# Business value model

**Status: scenario model, Phase 0. Not a forecast, not a quote, not a commitment.** The case study contains no revenue, cost, volume or baseline figure; the owner has supplied none, so **no input is user-provided**. Every other operating assumption is an illustrative scenario assumption with a stated rationale. The verified inputs are Azure **list prices** retrieved from the public Azure Retail Prices API; the benchmarks are published Singapore bunkering statistics used for scale. Results are **scenario figures** until the owner replaces the placeholders with measured data (D-034, BR-008).

Edit [model.json](model/model.json), then run `node harness/scripts/business-model.mjs --write`. The same arithmetic is shown below so a reviewer can reproduce any figure. Architecture context: [DES-0003](../architecture/designs/DES-0003-target-system-architecture.md), [TARGET-ARCHITECTURE](../target-architecture/README.md).

## Labels

| Label | Meaning | Inputs of this class in the model |
|---|---|---|
| verified | A priced meter from the Azure Retail Prices API (list price, USD, region southeastasia, retrieved 2026-10-29), or a public source that was read | 12 |
| user-provided | A figure given by a named person on a date | 0 |
| benchmark | A published figure with source, URL and retrieval date | 1 |
| scenario assumption | An illustrative placeholder with a rationale. Replace it | 79 |

A derived result takes the **weakest** class of the inputs it uses, so any result that depends on one scenario assumption is a scenario result. Conservative means low benefit and high cost; optimistic the reverse.

| Payback period (months; null = not within 10 years; years 4 to 10 held at year 3) | not within 10 years | 60.1 | 3.4 | scenario assumption |

Turnaround is in hours. Cost per certificate "today" is labour only. "Run cost" adds the platform operating cost per certificate at year 3 volume; "fully loaded" also spreads the one-time cost over three years of certificates. **Payback beyond three years is an extrapolation** that holds years 4 to 10 at year 3 values. ROI is net benefit divided by three-year TCO.

**Read the spread with care.** Each scenario moves every assumption the same way at once, so the conservative and optimistic columns are stacked extremes, not a confidence interval. They show how wide the unmeasured uncertainty is; they are not forecasts of a likely range. The base column is a placeholder for the owner's real numbers, not a prediction. Section 6 shows which single inputs drive the result.

## 5. Architecture options: what sovereignty costs

Cost only, same benefits for every option. **Option 1 is not eligible: it breaches HC-01** and is shown only so the price of sovereignty is visible. **Option 2 is conditional and not like-for-like:** its figures are a floor that omits the local processing and AI that residency requires, so it is shown for completeness and **no comparison or delta is drawn from it**. Only option 3 is a complete, eligible costing.

| Option | Eligible | Like-for-like? | Metric | Conservative | Base | Optimistic | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| opt1: Centralised Azure cloud | **no (HC-01)** | Same capability as option 3, but ineligible | One-time | $2,940,000 | $1,745,700 | $1,086,800 | scenario |
| opt1: Centralised Azure cloud | **no (HC-01)** | Same capability as option 3, but ineligible | Annual operating cost, year 3 | $486,448 | $305,680 | $203,585 | scenario |
| opt1: Centralised Azure cloud | **no (HC-01)** | Same capability as option 3, but ineligible | Three-year TCO | $4,399,132 | $2,662,569 | $1,697,369 | scenario |
| opt2: Jurisdiction-local edge plus one Azure shore platform | **conditional** | No: priced as a shore platform plus a local store per port. Calculation and AI over raw evidence would have to run at each port, and that is not priced | One-time | $4,027,500 | $2,427,075 | $1,542,200 | scenario |
| opt2: Jurisdiction-local edge plus one Azure shore platform | **conditional** | No: priced as a shore platform plus a local store per port. Calculation and AI over raw evidence would have to run at each port, and that is not priced | Annual operating cost, year 3 | $657,448 | $444,280 | $317,585 | scenario |
| opt2: Jurisdiction-local edge plus one Azure shore platform | **conditional** | No: priced as a shore platform plus a local store per port. Calculation and AI over raw evidence would have to run at each port, and that is not priced | Three-year TCO | $5,999,632 | $3,759,744 | $2,494,769 | scenario |
| opt3: Hybrid sovereign evidence cells with federated coordination | yes | Yes: full platform inside each jurisdiction | One-time | $4,027,500 | $2,283,325 | $1,353,000 | scenario |
| opt3: Hybrid sovereign evidence cells with federated coordination | yes | Yes: full platform inside each jurisdiction | Annual operating cost, year 3 | $1,731,091 | $985,308 | $668,457 | scenario |
| opt3: Hybrid sovereign evidence cells with federated coordination | yes | Yes: full platform inside each jurisdiction | Three-year TCO | $9,220,471 | $5,239,039 | $3,358,161 | scenario |

Price of sovereignty (option 3 minus option 1, three-year TCO): conservative $4,821,339; base $2,576,470; optimistic $1,660,792. This is the cost of keeping each jurisdiction's data in its jurisdiction against holding it in one place, in the model's scenario terms. Option 2 is not used for any delta: under HC-01 and SEC-003 raw evidence may be processed, and AI may run over it, only inside its originating jurisdiction, so option 2 would either need a local processing stack per port (approaching the cost of option 3 without its managed services) or confine agents to derived data and deliver less. Neither is priced.

## 7. Plausibility check

Group green-fuel tonnes in year 1 as a share of Singapore's 2025 biobunker sales (benchmark): conservative 10.9%; base 21.7%; optimistic 43.5%. The base volume is a large share of the largest bunkering port's biofuel market, which is generous. If the group's real volume is far lower, the volume-driven benefits fall in proportion; see the break-even row.

## 10. What would make this a real business case

Replace the highest-swing placeholders with measured figures first (D-034, BR-008). Ask the owner for these, in this order:

1. Claim, credit-note and discount history on green-fuel deliveries (drives the premium lines and the dispute lines).
2. Green-fuel deliveries, tonnes and invoiced premium per port and per month (drives volume and the premium pool).
3. Time-sheet or process-mining baseline for certificate assembly, calculation, approval and filing, per port.
4. Audit and certification-body fees and effort for the last two cycles.
5. Existing platform, licence and hosting costs that the platform would replace (none is credited in this model).
6. Per-port residency decisions (D-009, D-010), which fix how many cells are cloud and how many are on premises.

## 11. Limits

- Nothing here is verified except the Azure list prices at the retrieval date. A list price ignores agreements, reservations and discounts, and a price existing in a region does not mean the service meets any residency rule or is available in the zones needed.
- Prices are for one representative region. The price file holds eight Asian regions; list prices differ by region (see [azure-prices.json](model/azure-prices.json)).
- Benefits are not netted against the cost of the systems the platform would replace, and no avoided-incident or regulatory-penalty value is claimed.
- The model assumes the platform meets its functional requirements; it prices no rework from the open decisions.
- Premium and incremental-volume benefits are the least supported figures and are shown separately for that reason.
